dedupe_keys.name: helsinki metropolitan area 24 hour dynamic population from mobile phone data 250 m grid and neighbourhoods

description: Researchers of the Digital Geography Lab at the University of Helsinki, with the mobile operator Elisa, publish two open datasets of where people are in the Helsinki Metropolitan Area hour by hour, derived from aggregated mobile phone network data. The first (Bergroth et al., Scientific Data 9, 39, 2022) gives hourly population for regular workdays, Saturdays and Sundays on the 250 m statistical grid, assigning phone data to cells with dasymetric interpolation based on land cover, buildings and a time-use survey, validated against population and workplace registers. The second (Müürisepp et al., August 2026) uses 2021 data from a major operator to give hourly presence on an average weekday and weekend day by neighbourhood, linked to people's home neighbourhoods and weighted to Statistics Finland population data. Coverage: Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa and Kauniainen. Format and access: CSV and grid files in ZIP archives with a notebook, free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: averages of typical days, not events; one operator's subscribers weighted to the population; 2021 data reflect pandemic conditions. Simulation uses: exposure of people to hazards and to telecom and other service outages by hour, and agent-based and emergency response models. Related records: Flowminder's mobile phone population estimates and the Italian mobile network population dataset use similar methods.
